title: Fourier Tail Bound for Bounded Width DNF
statement: Let $d$ be a disjunctive normal form on $n$ Boolean variables, let $w,t\in\mathbb N$, and suppose the width of $d$ is at most $w$ and $w>0$. For the real-valued function $f$ that equals $-1$ where $d$ evaluates to true and $1$ where it evaluates to false, the Fourier weight on levels strictly above $120w(t+1)$ satisfies $\sum_{|S|>120w(t+1)}\widehat f(S)^2\le 8(1/2)^t$, with Fourier coefficients and expectation taken under the uniform cube measure.
hypotheses_covered: d is a DNF on n Boolean variables
The width of d is at most w
replaced: Let $d$ be a DNF on $n$ variables of width at most a positive integer $w$, and let $t\in\mathbb N$. Its sign encoding $f(x)=(-1)^{d(x)}$ satisfies $\sum_{|S|>120w(t+1)}\widehat f(S)^2\le8\,2^{-t}$ under the uniform cube law.
